text.p: Lehman Brothers said in a report released on Wednesday it was lowering its 1997 and 1998 earnings forecasts for Israel's largest supermarket chain Supersol Ltd but maintaining its 2 Outperform rating.

"We believe that near term, Supersol's earnings growth will be somewhat eroded by continuing losses in Super Office (its office supply chain). However, we believe the company will maintain its strong revenues growth ... and improve its earnings," analyst Elise Horowitz said.

Horowitz said she now forecast earnings per share (EPS) to reach 6.50 shekels this year, down from her previous forecast of 6.67 shekels. For 1998, she said, EPS would reach 7.29 shekels, down from an earlier estimate of 7.88 shekels.
Supersol earned 5.96 shekels per share in 1996.

Horowitz said she was lowering her forecast because of expenses connected with acquisition of the rival Shekem chain in February and continuing losses at Super Office. In the first quarter, Supersol reported earnings of 1.15 shekels a share, versus her 1.38 shekel estimate.
She said she was keeping to her target price of 11 shekels for Supersol's Tel Aviv-traded shares. Supersol closed on Tuesday at 10.35 shekels.
Horowitz said the company had no plans to acquire a stake in the Israeli do-it-yourself chain ACE or to enter the Romanian market as had been reported in the Israeli press.
